stories.headline: Bob Boone, part of MLB's 1st 3-generation family, dies at 78
stories.summary: Bob Boone, the catcher on the Phillies' first World Series title team who won seven Gold Gloves and was part of MLB's first three-generation family, has died.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Bob Boone, the catcher on the Philadelphia Phillies' first World Series championship team who won seven Gold Gloves and was part of baseball's first three-generation family, has died. He was 78.

Boone's son, Bret, announced his father's death Tuesday on social media. No cause of death was announced.

"He was a man of great integrity. He was a great dad, husband, and patriarch. It was a privilege to call him my father. Baseball lost a great one today," Bret Boone wrote.

Bob Boone spent his first 10 seasons with the Phillies, played seven with the California Angels and two with the Kansas City Royals. He also managed the Royals and Cincinnati Reds.

"Bob was an incredible player, teammate and family man," the Phillies said in a statement. "He embodied everything we believe exemplary athletes should represent, both on and off the field. We were proud to have him as part of the Phillies family during one of the most historic runs in team history. His impact on our organization, his teammates, and everyone who had the privilege of knowing him will never be forgotten.

MLB, in a statement, called the Boones "one of baseball's most historic families."

His father, Ray, played 13 seasons in the majors and was a two-time All-Star with the Detroit Tigers. Bob Boone's two sons both enjoyed long baseball careers: Aaron Boone played 13 seasons in the majors and played for the Reds when Bob managed the team; Bret Boone was a three-time All-Star over a 14-year career spent largely with the Seattle Mariners.

Aaron Boone now manages the New York Yankees.

"The Yankees mourn the passing of Bob Boone, who grew up in our sport and spent a lifetime giving back to the game he loved as an exceptional player, respected manager and distinguished executive," the team said in a statement. "His legacy is profound, and we can see the values he embodied carried forward by his son, Aaron, in his leadership of the Yankees."

A third son played in the minor leagues. Bret's son, Jake Boone, works in the New York Mets' front office after playing at Princeton and briefly in the minors.

Bob Boone was a sixth-round draft pick as a third baseman out of Stanford in 1969. He was converted to catcher in the minor leagues and caught 1,095 games with Philadelphia, second on the Phillies' all-time list to Red Dooin (1,124). Boone caught 2,225 games overall in 19 big league seasons.

He was the first Phillies catcher to win a Gold Glove (1978, 1979) and led the Phillies with a .412 batting average in their 1980 World Series win over the Royals.

"It was a sorrowful day [Monday] as we learned of the passing of Bob Boone, my teammate for over a decade, and friend for 50 years," Hall of Fame third baseman Mike Schmidt said in a statement. "We played in the minors together where he gave up third base so I could play it, only to become one of the best catchers in baseball history. ... Our lives and careers were intertwined, we pursued our Christian faith together, worked out together, and became world champions together. We lost a close friend. Rest in peace, Bob."

Boone made National League All-Star teams in 1976, 1978 and 1979. He set the record for career games caught by a catcher with 1,919 in Kansas City. He was 41 years old when he won his final Gold Glove with the Royals in 1989. Ivan Rodriguez and Carlton Fisk have since passed Boone on the career games caught list.

"Bob Boone was a leader, a manager, and our first Gold Glove winning catcher," the Royals said in a statement. "We honor his impact on our game, and send our thoughts and strength to his family."

Boone caught the final out of the 1980 Game 6 clincher when Tug McGraw struck out Willie Wilson to win the World Series. Boone was involved in a more famous play earlier in that inning when he ran after Frank White's foul pop near the home dugout in Veteran's Stadium. The ball bounced off Boone's mitt and straight into Pete Rose's glove for an out -- a catch played on countless highlight reels through the decades in Philadelphia.

He was added to the Phillies' Wall of Fame in 2005.

"Bob Boone was a quiet leader, both on and off the field," former Phillies teammate Larry Bowa said in a statement. "I had the privilege of playing alongside him for nearly my entire career, and without question, he was the backbone of our team."

Boone won four more Gold Gloves, made another All-Star team and twice led the Angels to the playoffs. He went 10-for-22 (.455) with a homer and two RBIs against Boston in the 1986 American League Championship Series.

"Boone's leadership, exceptional defense and knowledge of the game made him an invaluable presence behind the plate and helped the Angels win two division titles," the Angels said in a statement. "... His impact on our pitchers and the example he set for his teammates are lasting parts of his legacy with our franchise."

Boone went 371-444 overall as a manager, spending three seasons with the Royals and three with the Reds. He joined the Washington Nationals' front office in 2005.

Washington won the World Series in 2019, the first championship in franchise history. Boone resigned in 2021 rather than comply with the organization's COVID-19 vaccine mandate.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.summary: The NBA is back. The buzz never left. Bookmark this page for the latest news, rumblings and analysis from ESPN's insiders.
stories.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops.

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders.

ESPN's new NBA Trade Lab: Swing a deal!

Nov. 10

NBA Trade Lab updates: Former teammates join Luka in L.A.?
The Los Angeles Lakers find themselves at the top of the Western Conference standings, with Luka Doncic playing like the best player in the world and leading the way in ESPN's Net Points Metric (NBA Net Points Awards -- ESPN Analytics). Their BPI projected win total (2026-27 Projections NBA Power Index -- ESPN) that started the season at 45 has already increased to 53. They completely retooled their roster this past offseason after losing LeBron James in free agency to the Philadelphia 76ers, but their newly added pieces have jelled together quickly to leave fans around the league rethinking what the ceiling of this team could be.

After sending out two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the Walker Kessler sign-and-trade (Lakers trade for Jazz C Walker Kessler, sign trio, sources say -- ESPN), the Lakers are very limited in remaining draft capital they could use to add another major piece through a trade. However, this hasn't stopped Lakers fans from diving into our NBA Trade Lab tool to cook up some mock trades in an attempt to find the Lakers another piece around the margins that could complete this roster for a deep playoff run.

Trade No. 1
Lakers get: P.J. Washington

Washington is a versatile two-way wing who started alongside Doncic during the Mavericks' run to the finals in 2024. Washington played the best basketball of his career alongside Luka during their time together on the Mavs (P.J. Washington-- NBA Net Points) and would be a proven contributor to add to the Lakers' depth.

Dallas Mavericks get: Jarred Vanderbilt, Cameron Carr, and two second-round picks

Carr, the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, is a promising young player the Mavericks can plug in right away and develop around their young core. The two second-round picks would also be a welcome addition for Dallas, which currently doesn't have any second-round picks (outside of a top-55 protected Hawks' 2027 second-rounder).

Trade No. 2

Lakers get: Jalen Smith

Smith is a young intriguing stretch big, whose advanced metrics paint as a positive player even on a middling Chicago Bulls team. Despite averaging only 17 minutes a game in his career, Smith possesses a rare blend of rim defense, rebounding and 3-point shooting. This would be a buy-low opportunity for the Lakers to invest in the potential of Smith, letting him play off one of the best playmakers in the world in Luka Doncic.

Chicago Bulls get: Jaden Hardy and two second-round picks

If the Bulls aren't as convinced about Smith's potential or are unsure of what kind of an extension they would give him this upcoming summer, they could decide to trade him before the deadline rather than lose him for nothing.

Trade No. 3
Lakers get: Derrick Jones Jr

Jones is a talented defender who also started alongside Luka Doncic during the Mavericks' 2024 Finals run. He was an unsung hero throughout that 2024 playoff run as he held his own on defense against the likes of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Anthony Edwards. His thin frame combined with outlier athleticism (Derrick Jones Jr. edges Aaron Gordon in controversial dunk contest -- ESPN) allows him to navigate around screens and successfully shadow the shiftiest superstars in a way that few others in the league can. His addition to the Lakers as a reliable point-of-attack defender would be immensely helpful in slowing down an opposing star guard in a playoff series.

LA Clippers get: Jaden Hardy and three second-round picks

The Clippers' future draft assets are severely depleted after the NBA stripped them of five future first-round picks (NBA announces punishments for Clippers after Kawhi inquiry -- ESPN) for circumventing the salary cap. It makes sense for the Clippers to try to parlay any valuable veteran players on their current roster to start to recoup some future draft capital.

Have any ideas on what move the Lakers should make? Build it in the NBA Trade Lab, then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides. -- Ben Tiemeyer

Nov. 9

NBA Trade Lab updates: The latest Sabonis deals
As my colleague Ben Tiemeyer wrote earlier, Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis is the player most involved in fan-created trades in the new NBA Trade Lab. While Porzingis has the most interest, trading for Sacramento Kings center Domantas Sabonis could be the most impactful.

The Kings sit in the bottom of the Western Conference standings and have prioritized building their roster with young players, notably lottery pick Darius Acuff Jr. They have gone from one of the oldest rosters in the NBA last season to a team with seven players 26 years old or younger this season.

Sabonis was named All-NBA in 2024 and appeared in 82 games. However, last season he played the fewest games (19) in his career and had season ending knee surgery in February.

Sabonis has two years and $94 million left on his contract ($45.5 and $48.6 million).

Below are some of the top fan-created trades involving Sabonis, as scored by fans voting from the perspective of each team involved:

Trade No. 1

Kings get: A top-4 protected first from a rebuilding Chicago is strong value for the Kings. Nic Claxton gives Sacramento a serviceable center with two years left on his contract. The negative is the $18 million owed to Patrick Williams in 2028-29.

Chicago Bulls get: The addition of Sabonis still puts Chicago in a position to use cap space next summer. The Bulls could also flip Norman Powell in a separate trade if needed. The downside is a rebuilding team losing a lightly protected first in 2028.

Trade No. 2

Kings get: RJ Barrett is on pace to average 20 points but is on an expiring contract. The Kings could extend him before becoming a free agent. The Jakob Poeltl contract is not ideal considering there are three years left after this season. The Kings are getting a first-round pick involved, but that is top-16 protected.

Toronto Raptors get: A double-double presence in Sabonis to pair with Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard. The danger comes with Toronto entering the luxury tax next season.

Trade No. 3

Kings get: The prize asset out of this trade is the 2027 top-14 protected first from Miami. If the Heat do not make the playoffs, the pick becomes unprotected. The Kings take a flier on former lottery pick Tidjane Salaun. His fourth-year team option was recently declined.

Charlotte Hornets get: This trade does not fit the conservative approach Charlotte has taken with its roster. But Sabonis gives it a former All-Star to pair with Brandon Miller. The concern is the trade pushing Charlotte closer to the luxury tax next season.

Have any more ideas on what move the Kings should make? Build it in the NBA Trade Lab, then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides. -- Bobby Marks

Windhorst on whether fatigue will cost Wembanyama and the Spurs this season: "He said playing this way is exhausting to him. Going in there and fighting and playing this way is exhausting him. And in this game that he had, which went down to the very end against the Mavericks, he was exhausted at the end of the game. And this is something we saw in the playoffs last year where they had a difficult time evening out his energy, saving his energy. We saw them throughout the Finals, essentially trying to figure out a way to keep his energy going. So when he says it tires him out too much, we should pay attention to that and be aware.

"Having said that, I know that he wants to shoot from the outside. We know that that's something he's wanted to do his whole life. Well, he's shooting 24% on 3s so far this year. But what he's saying is because he's struggling shooting the outside shot, he's going inside more."

Iger's son Will to be part of Lakers' G League broadcast
The Los Angeles Lakers' G League affiliate has a new name, a new home, a new coach and a new broadcasting team for the upcoming season.

The Coachella Valley Lakers, previously the South Bay Lakers, announced Thursday that Will Iger will be their play-by-play announcer for the upcoming season, with former Lakers big man A.C. Green returning as the color analyst on Spectrum SportsNet.

Iger joins Coachella Valley after calling games for the Austin Toros, the San Antonio Spurs' G League affiliate, last season. He has also done studio work for the Dallas Mavericks and play-by-play for San Antonio FC.

He is the son of incoming Lakers co-owner Bob Iger and Willow Bay, former co-host of the popular "NBA Inside Stuff" television show with Ahmad Rashad.

Coachella Valley will open its season Friday against the Salt Lake City Stars in Palm Desert, California, at Acrisure Arena.

It will be Alex Cerda's first game roaming the sideline after being hired in September as CVL's head coach. Cerda served as an assistant for South Bay under Zach Guthrie and was bumped up after Guthrie was added to Lakers coach JJ Redick's staff.

Wemby makes MVP opening statement
Victor Wembanyama officially launched his 2027 NBA MVP campaign on Wednesday with a statistical performance not seen since Wilt Chamberlain.

The Spurs star posted 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks in a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, becoming the first player to achieve a 52/24/8 line since blocks became an official statistic in 1973-74.

Chamberlain, the Hall of Fame center, is the only player in league history to match or exceed those numbers thanks to a 55-point, 29-rebound, 17-block performance for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in 1961.

This was truly rare air: Wembanyama posted the NBA's first 52/24 line since Chamberlain in 1969 and the first 50-20 game since Luka Doncic in 2022.

"It should be more like this," Wembanyama promised. "More often."

With Doncic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander emerging as early MVP favorites, Wembanyama threw his hat into the ring on a wild night that easily could have gotten even wilder. The 2023 No. 1 pick set a new career high for scoring by shooting 16-of-28 from the field and 19-of-23 from the free throw line against an overmatched Dallas front line, but he made only one of his eight 3-point attempts.

"I can still do more," Wembanyama said, noting that he's shooting a career-low 24 percent on 3-pointers this season. "My shots weren't falling tonight and that forces me into a style of play that is exhausting. I can do it. The proof is there."

After stumbling out of the gate with an 0-2 start, the Spurs have won six straight games and Wembanyama has started to find his scoring groove. The Thunder held the French center to 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting on opening night, but he has scored at least 36 points in three of his past four games and is on track to lead the NBA in blocks for the fourth straight season.

Go ahead and brace for more fireworks: Wembanyama and the Spurs are set to face the NBA's three worst defenses -- the Kings, Suns and Bulls -- over the next week.

Wembanyama, 22, finished third in MVP voting last season and is seeking to become the award's youngest winner since Derrick Rose in 2011. -- Ben Golliver

Nov. 4

NBA Trade Lab updates: Porzingis is popular in mock deals
In the first weeks since the release of ESPN Analytics' new NBA Trade Lab, the player involved in the most fan-created trades is Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis, who's in the news because the franchise is withholding payments from him while he's away from the team.

With 38-year-old legend Stephen Curry still playing at an elite level, it makes sense that fans want to see the Warriors make a swing to bolster his supporting cast. Add to that how good rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has looked to start the season, and Warriors fans might be right to think their favorite team isn't that far away from contention in the West, especially considering the early-season injury problems for the Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves.

Porzingis' $20 million salary would be a key ingredient for the Warriors to match salary in a potential trade.

Below are some of the top fan-created trades involving Porzingis, as scored by fans voting from the perspective of each team involved:

Trade No. 1

Warriors get: A shot-blocking stretch big in Myles Turner who could be a great fit in their motion-heavy offense to replicate some of Porzingis' game.

Milwaukee Bucks get: Porzingis and a young promising player in Moses Moody, who could be more valuable for the Bucks' rebuild. Moody is recovering from a torn left patellar tendon he suffered in March.

Trade No. 2

Warriors get: Daniel Gafford, who can provide rim protection and elite play-finishing. He would bolster their center depth and better exploit defenses that are stretched thin out on the perimeter drawn to Curry's gravity.
Dallas Mavericks get: Porzingis and a first-round pick swap to help reset their timeline around 19-year-old centerpiece Cooper Flagg, by improving their assets in a potentially loaded 2028 draft.

Trade No. 3

Warriors get: Talented 6-foot-8 forward Trey Murphy III, who can defend, draw fouls and rain 3s from well beyond the arc. At 26 years old, he also has the potential to be paired alongside Lendeborg as the wing duo of the future in the post-Curry era.

New Orleans Pelicans get: Porzingis, a promising young player in Moody and two future first-round picks to cash in on Murphy's value. Doing this deal would also provide more on-ball opportunities for 2025 lottery picks Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen.

Have any more ideas on what move the Warriors should make? Build them in the NBA Trade Lab, then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides. -- Ben Tiemeyer

How Dybantsa will impact the Wizards on the court

After missing the first four games of the season with an ankle injury, No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa will make his regular-season debut Wednesday, ESPN's Shams Charania reported.

Dybantsa's arrival could give the Wizards one of the best starting lineups in the Eastern Conference -- which would be quite a change of pace for a team that hasn't won 20 games in a season since 2022-23. What are the Warriors' options on Porzingis?

ESPN's Anthony Slater detailed the Golden State Warriors' options regarding center Kristaps Porzingis and his lingering health issues in a report today.

[Stephen] Curry twice made sure to mention the human component, expressing sympathy for Porzingis, who has made public the lingering impact he said he still feels after contracting an upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics two seasons ago.

"We always said availability was a big factor for our team with all the guys we have out," Curry said. "It's no secret that the [center] spot is an important one for us, especially with his skill set. It's hard to talk about without keeping the humanity of it in mind. But it is a tough one to figure out."

Team sources continue to express an extreme level of pessimism that Porzingis will ever play for the Warriors again, but he could end up helping the organization in another way, because his contract, which is only guaranteed for $3 million next season, could still prove to be valuable in executing a trade.

Marks on the Thunder's next steps following crucial injuries: "I think the long term, Brian and Tim, is that you will apply for this disabled player exception for Jalen Williams. I don't think you'll get it for Cason Wallace because you have to be deemed out until June 15. And I don't think that Wallace injury will get you there. I think the Jalen Williams injury will. Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected
The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Xavi Simons reveals emotional toll of Spurs ACL injury as return nears
stories.summary: Injured Tottenham attacker Xavi Simons has spoken of the anguish he felt watching the club's relegation battle last season, but is working "endless hours" to return for Roberto De Zerbi's side.
stories.body:
Injured Tottenham attacker Xavi Simons has spoken of the anguish he felt watching the club's relegation battle last season, but is working "endless hours" to return for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

Xavi sustained anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) damage during a 1-0 win at Wolves on April 25 which ruled the Netherlands playmaker out of Spurs' final four fixtures along with the World Cup last summer.

However, Xavi, 23, has been ahead of schedule through his rehabilitation and is set to enter phase three of his recovery later in November, which will allow him to resume team training.

Last month, the former Barcelona and Paris St Germain youngster was invited to speak at the Oxford Union and went into detail about his current spell on the sidelines.

Speaking on Oct. 30, Xavi told students: "I had to watch the remainder of the season from my hospital bed and let me tell you it was not easy.

"I felt completely out of control, infuriated because I couldn't contribute and help. I couldn't do a thing. Luckily the boys did their job.

"Mental is just as important as physical. I've had bad moments at night, not even my family know how bad. I've cried, I've wanted so bad to contribute to Spurs, to my national team.

"I read books, I enhanced my knowledge on certain things, I wanted more information, I wanted to stimulate my mind. I wanted calmness in my brain. That was as important as going to the gym every day.

- Tottenham's winning run brought to abrupt end by late Noah Okafor winner

- Leeds condemn 'disgusting' alleged racist abuse of Jayden Bogle after Spurs game

"It's ultimately finding the balance. You can't underestimate the importance of good psychological health. If your brain isn't working, your body isn't working."

ACL ruptures generally have a recovery time of around nine months, but Xavi is in line to feature in first-team training again after the international break.

That would put him back in contact training only seven months after suffering the injury and raises the possibility of a return to competitive action before the nine-month mark at the end of January.

Quizzed during a question-and-answer session about how he plans to return at his best, Xavi said: "My knee has to feel good. I need to feel strong. Right now, I'm on track, I'm getting stronger every day.

"I'm putting in endless hours. I have a great team that has been with me this entire journey. Everyone has a different schedule.

"Everyone's journey is different. For me, I want to come home and only think, 'I can't move my legs anymore,' because I have pushed myself to the limit daily.

"I want to feel tired. That feeling is when I allow myself to rest. That's how I've approached it throughout."

stories.headline: NHL Awards Watch: Believe it or not, McDavid not the unanimous MVP pick right now
stories.summary: Our panel of PHWA voters identify their finalists for all the awards, with some tight races in a few spots.
stories.body:
There are clear favorites for NHL awards after the first month-plus of the regular season -- and some of them don't actually play for the Edmonton Oilers.

Yes, Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard had proved to be undeniable awards contenders out of the gate. But it's also undeniable that front-runners at the start of the season might not be the players holding trophies at the end of the season.

Welcome to the NHL Awards Watch for November. We've polled a wide selection of Professional Hockey Writers Association voters anonymously to get a sense of where the wind is blowing for the current leaders. We've made sure it's a cross section from the entire league, trying to gain as many perspectives as possible.

Keep in mind that the PHWA votes for the Hart, Norris, Calder, Selke and Lady Byng finalists, broadcasters vote for the Jack Adams and general managers vote for the Vezina.

All stats are from Hockey-Reference.com, Natural Stat Trick and Evolving Hockey.

Jump ahead:

Ross | Richard | Hart

Norris | Selke | Vezina

Calder | Byng | Adams

Art Ross Trophy (points leader)
Click here for the updated point-scoring standings.

Maurice 'Rocket' Richard Trophy
Click here for the updated goal-scoring standings.

Hart Trophy (MVP)
Leader: Connor McDavid, Edmonton Oilers

Finalists: Kirill Kaprizov, Minnesota Wild; Nathan MacKinnon, Colorado Avalanche

"Duh."

"Really, is there anyone else?"

"He's the clear front-runner and it's not close."

Yes, the reviews are in for McDavid's first several weeks of the 2026-27 season. The Oilers' star earned just over 88% of the first-place votes on our MVP ballots.

McDavid is seeking his fourth Hart Trophy and first since 2023, which is an odd gap in MVP honors for a player who is constantly in the conversation. Only three players in NHL history won the Hart Trophy four times: Wayne Gretzky, as part of his NHL record nine MVP honors, as well as Gordie Howe and Eddie Shore.

The Oilers' center had 47 points in his first 18 games this season. To put that points pace into perspective: His 2.61 points-per-game average would rank as the sixth highest in a single season, with only three Gretzky campaigns and two Mario Lemieux scoring seasons ranking ahead of him. That McDavid offensive fuel has made Edmonton a top-five team since the start of the season.

As one awards voter noted: Bookmakers have "the field" at plus money vs. McDavid when it comes to the MVP race. That's how heavy a favorite he is right now.

That said, the Hart Trophy vote was not unanimous among those we surveyed.

MacKinnon received first-place support and consistent mentions lower on the ballots. The star center won the Hart in 2024 and has been a finalist five times, including a third-place finish last season. The Avalanche haven't gotten off the blocks how they wanted this season, but that's not on MacKinnon. He had 30 points through 18 games, seven more than any other teammate.

Completing a Western Conference sweep of the Hart finalists: Wild winger Kaprizov. He had 31 points through 19 games to start the season, and his 16 goals were near the top of that leaderboard. His line with Joel Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy has been the best in the league, rolling to nearly five goals per 60 minutes at 5-on-5 while not surrendering an even-strength goal through 19 games.

Kaprizov has never been a Hart Trophy finalist in his career, and has finished in the top 10 in MVP voting only once in six seasons. Like MacKinnon, he had first-place support and a ton of love down the ballot.

"I wouldn't bet against Kirill Kaprizov narrowing the gap as the season goes along," one McDavid voter warned.

Another name mentioned by our MVP voters was Edmonton's Evan Bouchard ... but we believe he has designs on another trophy at the moment.

Norris Trophy (top defenseman)
Leader: Evan Bouchard, Edmonton Oilers

Finalist: Quinn Hughes, Minnesota Wild; Zach Werenski, Columbus Blue Jackets

Bouchard is the runaway favorite for the Norris right now with over 83% of the first-place votes, for the same reason McDavid is leading for the Hart: At some point, the stats just become undeniable.

The Oilers' defenseman had 31 points through his first 18 games, following a dominating 95-point season in 2025-26. He had a plus-25 rating last season. He's already at plus-24 this season.

"The electric offense pace is too much to ignore, even if there are still some defensive lapses," a Bouchard voter said.

Bouchard, who was fourth for the Norris last season, has faced the same obstacle that other offensive defensemen have faced in trying to win this award: whether his defensive game is Norris-worthy. The same clips of blown coverages that used to dog players such as Erik Karlsson have burned into the memories of voters when it comes to Bouchard. But that perception seems to be changing; or, at the very least, his offensive game is so overwhelming that it silences that defensive debate. (See also: Karlsson, Erik.)

"Bouchard is on pace for 67 points before Santa drops his gifts off under the tree. Plus, he isn't anywhere near the defensive liability many like to suggest," another Bouchard backer boasted.

"Bouchard has a slight edge over Quinn Hughes because of overall production. But it's hard to argue Hughes hasn't been terrific in handling a significant workload," another noted.

Hughes earned the second-most first-place votes and is the clear second choice in this race. The Norris winner in 2023, Hughes is averaging 28 minutes, 7 seconds in ice time per game for the Wild. Despite Bouchard's blockbuster offensive season, Hughes is right there with him in the scoring race among defensemen with 26 points through his first 19 games. He has been a driving force behind the Wild's successful start.

Hughes was seventh for the Norris last season, when he split his time between Minnesota and Vancouver.

"To me, he's the biggest difference-maker from the back end in the league, just dangerous in so many ways," a Hughes voter beamed.

The only other defenseman to earn a first-place vote was Werenski, who won the Norris for the first time last season. He has 14 points through 15 games, skating to a plus-6 and averaging a league-high 28:18 per game in ice time. Unlike the other two finalists here, Werenski's team is off to a disappointing start, but he has been a highlight among lowlights.

Other defensemen mentioned for the Norris by our voters included Adam Fox of the New York Rangers, Cale Makar of the Colorado Avalanche and Mikhail Sergachev of the Utah Mammoth.

Calder Trophy (top rookie)
Leader: Jacob Fowler, Montreal Canadiens

Finalists: Michael Brandsegg-Nygard, Detroit Red Wings; Roman Kantserov, Chicago Blackhawks

The Calder Trophy race has one clear favorite above a disparate collection of rookies making impacts in a variety of ways for their teams.

Let's start with the big name in flashing lights on the marquee. Fowler, 21, is a Florida native who has quickly established himself as the goalie of the future for the Montreal Canadiens ... only a few months after Montreal appeared to have found its goalie of the future.

"Wasn't the net supposed to belong to Jakub Dobes?" a Fowler voter asked.

Fowler was 8-1-1 in his first 10 games this season, with a .925 save percentage and a 2.15 goals-against average. Money Puck had him second in the NHL goals saved above expected through those games (11.4). His two shutouts led all rookie goalies. He's been phenomenal for Montreal.

The Canadiens netminder earned just over 61% of the first-place votes for the Calder. He's trying to become the first goalie to win the Calder since Steve Mason of the Blue Jackets in 2008-09. But he's also looking over his shoulder at a deep freshman class.

"This rookie race is insane," another Fowler voter declared. "Tough to pinpoint a real favorite."

Earning the second-most first-place votes: Brandsegg-Nygård of the Red Wings. The 21-year-old Norwegian was drafted 15th overall in 2024 and played 14 games with Detroit last season. This season, he had 10 points through 18 games with a three-plus minute jump in ice time.

"Even more impressive than his points was that Detroit outscored teams 12-3 with him on the ice and without him were outscored 18-27," a Brandsegg-Nygård voter explained.

The player with the next highest total of first-place votes is also a bright spot on a mediocre team: Roman Kantserov, the 22-year-old Russian-born winger for the Blackhawks. He led the KHL in goals last season before signing with the Blackhawks, who drafted him 44th overall in 2023.

He scored nine goals in his first 18 NHL games to go along with two assists. Kantserov was the leading goal scorer on the Blackhawks, who ranked last in the league offensively heading into Monday's action.

"I'm leaning toward Kantserov. He's playing big minutes and producing, albeit for a hapless Chicago team," one of his voters acknowledged.

Other rookies to get first-place votes included 2026 first overall pick Gavin McKenna of the Toronto Maple Leafs; Vegas Golden Knights forward Trevor Connelly, who's been near the top of the rookie scoring leaders; Boston Bruins forward James Hagens, another name near the top of the scoring leaderboard who has produced solid numbers in limited minutes; and Rangers goalie Dylan Garand, who was thrust into action when Igor Shesterkin was lost for the season to a knee injury.

Vezina Trophy (top goaltender)
Note: The NHL's general managers vote for this award.

Leader: Jesper Wallstedt, Minnesota Wild

Finalists: Pyotr Kochetkov, Carolina Hurricanes; Linus Ullmark, Ottawa Senators

Wallstedt finished sixth for the Calder last season but is the current leader for the Vezina among our voters. The "Wall of St. Paul" is 11-2-3 in his first 16 games, with a .922 save percentage and a 1.99 goals-against average; analytically, Money Puck has Wallstedt as the league leader in goals saved above expected (13.3) through 16 games.

"He's been outstanding while facing a lot of quality chances," a voter noted.

"Wallstedt is my front-runner right now. He's been a workhorse and has backed it up (two or fewer goals allowed in 11 of 16 starts)," another stated.

Wallstedt earned around 58% of the first-place votes. The next-highest total belonged to Kochetkov, who has put up stellar numbers while starting 12 of the Hurricanes' 19 games. The 27-year-old might be finally breaking through after several seasons in the Canes' goaltending mix. He has a .920 save percentage and a 1.67 goals-against average through 12 games.

The goalie with the next-most first-place votes is Linus Ullmark of the Senators. But, admittedly, this was a surprise given that he's been limited to just eight games due to injury. But within those eight games, no one was better this season: 7-1-0 with a .945 save percentage and a 1.33 goals-against average.

"Linus Ullmark probably would be the leader here if not for the injury he suffered," a Wallstedt voter argued.

Only one other goalie received first-place support from our voters: Boston Bruins netminder Jeremy Swayman. He's 9-3-1 in 13 games this season, with a .920 save percentage and a 2.21 goals-against average. Swayman was a finalist for this award last season.

"This is Swayman at his best. No way Boston is this good out of the gate without him playing at this level," a Swayman backer declared.

Other goalies who received support down the ballot included Montreal's Jacob Fowler and Dallas' Jake Oettinger.

Selke Trophy (best defensive forward)
Leader: Joel Eriksson Ek, Minnesota Wild

Finalists: Anthony Cirelli, Tampa Bay Lightning; Nick Suzuki, Montreal Canadiens

It's been a minute since Eriksson Ek was a Selke darling. After finishing fourth for the award in 2021, he was outside the top 10 finishers for the award in the last two seasons. Naturally, he's the early leader for the defensive forward award while having one of his best offensive starts, because that's how the Selke works. Eriksson Ek has 17 points in 19 games, skating to a plus-16.

"The Wild have given up just two goals in more than 260 minutes with him on the ice at 5 on 5, and none in over 200 minutes at full strength when he's centering Kaprizov and Boldy," one voter revealed.

Eriksson Ek led the voting with 26% of the first-place votes. But as usual with the Selke, there's a robust collection of forwards that also earned first-place love.

Suzuki and Cirelli were tied with just over 15% of the first-place votes. It was Suzuki's turn to win the Selke last season, in which he also finished fifth for the Hart Trophy. He's been impactful again for the Habs despite being limited to 11 games due to injury.

If it's any player's "turn" to win the Selke this season, it might be Cirelli. He finished third in the voting in 2025 and then second to Suzuki last season.

"He's just so consistent," a Cirelli voter argued.

The only other player to receive multiple first-place votes was Sebastian Aho of the Carolina Hurricanes. Would it be weird if Jordan Staal remains without a Selke win in his career but Aho collects one instead for Carolina?

Other players receiving first-place votes were Montreal center Phillip Danault; Vegas center Jack Eichel; Dallas center Radek Faksa; Boston center Elias Lindholm; and Vancouver center Elias Pettersson. Other players that were mentioned down the ballot included New Jersey center Nico Hischier and Philadelphia forward Noah Cates.

Lady Byng Trophy (gentlemanly play)

This is the part where I mention that the Lady Byng Trophy for gentlemanly play should be voted on by the league's on-ice officials or by the NHL Players' Association instead of the PHWA. Traditionally, this award goes to a player with a top-20 point total and the lowest penalty minutes among those players.

Jack Hughes has 25 points in 18 games and has yet to take a penalty this season. Works for us.

Jack Adams Award (best coach)
Note: The NHL Broadcasters' Association votes on this award.

Leader: Marco Sturm, Boston Bruins

Finalists: Rod Brind'Amour, Carolina Hurricanes; Travis Green, Ottawa Senators

The Bruins are one of the NHL's biggest surprises this season, and Sturm is getting much of the credit. The second-year head coach has them playing to a plus-27 goal differential and earned 58% of the first-place votes on our ballots.

"He probably should've gotten more love last year," a Sturm backer argued.

"Every year I expect the Bruins to drop off the map, but they continue to chart a course toward the playoffs. And when you look at this roster, it doesn't scream top of the Atlantic Division, and yet, here we are," another explained.

The second-most first-place votes belong to Brind'Amour, who has the Hurricanes atop the Metro Division after winning the Stanley Cup last season. They remain defensively stout, but Brind'Amour has them cooking offensively: Through 19 games, the Hurricanes led the league in goals per game.

"Is putting the defending Stanley Cup champion coach as the Jack Adams frontrunner too cliche? Oh well, I'm doing it," one voter joked.

Brind'Amour has coached through some adversity, having lost captain Jordan Staal to injury last month.

Green has coached the Senators through much more of it, from losing Brady Tkachuk to an offseason trade to a slew of injuries that befell the Ottawa roster early on this season.

Despite all that, the Senators were in a wild-card spot after 18 games.

"Ottawa keeps taking its lumps, and Green is somehow keeping them in the mix. Impressive," one voter concluded.

Two other coaches received first-place votes: Montreal Canadiens bench boss Martin St. Louis and Mike Babcock of the Edmonton Oilers.

That Babcock didn't receive more support is both surprising and unsurprising. On the one hand, he's overseen a torrid start for the Oilers in which McDavid is amassing points at a historic pace while the team plays solid defense in front of uncharacteristically strong goaltending. On the other hand, Babcock carried significant baggage into this job and the voters -- at least among the writers -- have a long memory.

"Babcock could go 84-0 and he would not get my vote," a Sturm voter revealed.

stories.headline: Qatar, Abu Dhabi races set to go ahead as F1 rules out Imola backup plan for finale
stories.summary: Formula 1 has told Imola it will not be required to hold a season-ending race, meaning the plan to finish 2026 in Qatar and Abh Dhabi is now set in stone.
stories.body:
Formula 1 has told Imola it will not be required to hold a season-ending race, meaning the plan to finish 2026 in Qatar and Abh Dhabi is now set in stone barring unforeseen circumstances.

F1 had created a backup plan to finish the season in Italy on Dec. 6 in case hostilities resumed in the Middle East after the U.S. midterms.

The Italian circuit had started building grandstands but needed to know whether to commit to full-scale preparations.

On Tuesday, the deadline reported by ESPN last week, F1 has now let Imola know it will not be required.

It means as things stand, F1's season finishes with a triple header of races in Las Vegas on Nov. 21, Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6.

Formula 1 has repeatedly stressed that it has been in constant communication with governments in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, while also monitoring travel advice from relevant European countries where the sport's 11 teams are based.

F1 was emboldened by the fact that MotoGP, also owned by Liberty Media, last weekend raced without issue in the Qatar circuit hosting F1 at the end of this month.

MotoGP team Yamaha pulled out of that event due to the company's global travel policy.

No F1 team has similar restrictions about travelling to the region.

The Imola news means F1 is full-speed ahead with its original schedule plan.

Sources have told ESPN that the final two races can still be scrapped if there were renewed hostilities in the Middle East.

Sources have confirmed in that instance, without Imola, that would mean the season ending with the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

- McLaren's Piastri splits from ex-F1 driver Webber's management team

- Mercedes new era of dominance? Wolff warns of fight to retain constructors'

- Verstappen's P21 to P2: Red Bull a 'disaster to drive' in São Paulo

From a sporting context, both championships are settled -- Kimi Antonelli won the drivers' championship in Mexico, while Mercedes wrapped up the constructors' in Brazil. However, the constructors' championship is how teams are allocated their prize money and plenty of other teams are fighting for positions lower down.

Sources have told ESPN that F1's commercial agreement with the teams states there must be 22 races minimum in a calendar year, although their commercial agreements with broadcasters will be satisfied at the conclusion Las Vegas' event.

The U.S. and Israeli war in Iran earlier in the year forced F1 to cancel April races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, although Bahrain paid to reschedule with an event at Malaysian circuit in October.

Despite the rescheduled Bahrain race, were the final two races to be cancelled, F1 would be left with 21 races for the season.

stories.headline: Tatiana Suarez secures top-3 spot, positions herself for strawweight title shot
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Tatiana Suarez and Virna Jandiroba have traded places in the ESPN strawweight rankings -- something they did not do in their UFC fight on Saturday.

Suarez piled up 9 minutes, 12 seconds of control time -- well more than half of the fight -- when she met Jandiroba in what amounted to a title eliminator. With the unanimous decision victory, Suarez moves up one spot to No. 3 in the 115-pound rankings. She's right behind UFC champion Mackenzie Dern, whom she hopes to fight next in a title bout.

Jandiroba, who fended off all nine of Suarez's takedown attempts but nonetheless couldn't escape her opponent's smothering control, drops to No. 4.

The only other change in the divisional rankings is at heavyweight, where Waldo Cortes Acosta drops from the top 10 after being knocked out over the weekend by Johnny Walker. Rizvan Kuniev moves up to the No. 9 position formerly occupied by Cortes Acosta, and Vitor Petrino enters the rankings at No. 10.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

Results are current; rankings as of Nov. 10. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

HEAVYWEIGHT (up to 265 pounds)

stories.headline: Ex-San Diego FC forward Cédric Bakambu files fair housing lawsuit
stories.summary: Former San Diego FC forward Cédric Bakambu has filed a housing discrimination lawsuit in federal court.
stories.body:
Former San Diego FC forward Cédric Bakambu has filed a housing discrimination lawsuit in federal court against one real estate firm, two property owners and two real estate agents, according to information contained in the filing.

The lawsuit, a copy of which has been viewed by ESPN, alleges the defendants discriminated against Bakambu and his wife, Anne-Laure Hueber, on the basis of "familial status" by denying them the opportunity rent a house because they had children who would be living with them.

According to the lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California, the individuals and entities listed as defendants are property owners JW Wealth and Sheila Nasehi, real estate firm Compass California III and Compass agents Gillian Gillies and Bree Bornstein.

Neither Major League Soccer nor San Diego FC are named as a defendant in the lawsuit.

Bakambu and Hueber are seeking unspecified compensatory, statutory and punitive damages, as well as declaratory and injunctive relief, attorney's fees and costs under the Fair Housing Act, the California Fair Employment and Housing Act and the Unruh Civil Rights Act.

Bakambu signed with San Diego FC back on Sept. 3, and in nine matches for SDFC, he scored four goals with one assist.

In an Instagram post dated Nov. 6, Bakambu, a Congo DR international who played at last summer's World Cup, announced that he would no longer be playing for San Diego, stating, "Some decisions are beyond our control."

A request for comment from a representative for JW Wealth wasn't successful. A request for comment from Compass was also not successful.

ESPN has asked San Diego FC, MLS and the MLS Players' Association for comment.

The suit, which was filed on Monday, alleged two instances of discrimination. In the first alleged incident, Bakambu made an offer to rent a 5,679 square-foot house in San Diego, Calif. for a monthly rent of $17,500.

The filing details how Gillies, the agent representing Compass, stated that a pool barrier "would be required due to the age of the children" and asked whether Bakambu would pay an estimated $6,000 to install it if the owner approved.

Alternatives were proposed by Bakambu's broker, Sandra Shebani, including mesh covers and splash alarms.

Gillies responded: "A barrier will need to be installed."

The requirement wasn't mentioned in the property listing.

By Sept. 16, Bakambu made an updated offer that included paying a year's rent in advance, a Pool and Spa Liability Addendum, and an agreement to pay for the barrier.

According to the filing, Compass managing director Melanie Fontana later told Shebani that another applicant that met the lease requirements was under consideration, that Bakambu's offer had been received and that the owner would fund any pool safety measures.

The lawsuit goes on to state that on Sept. 18, 2026, Ms. Shebani raised the fair-housing concern directly with Kathy Mehringer, Compass's Broker of Record and Managing Director of Compliance and Risk Management.

Mehringer responded: "Melanie has explained the process. Compass is not violating any fair housing rules - why would you accuse us of doing so? That is not collaboration."

The filing states that Bakambu's offer was never accepted, and the rental listing was withdrawn from the market after his real estate agent raised fair-housing concerns with Compass management. The suit states that by tying rental conditions to the children and their ages, Bakambu and Hueber were discriminated against.

Later, Bakambu and Hueber sought to rent a 6,300 square-foot house through Compass in Rancho Sante Fe, Calif., and on Oct. 11, 2026, after viewing the property with Bornstein, offered a monthly rent of $23,500.

The filing states: "The offer and follow-up from Ms. Hueber went unanswered even after Plaintiffs observed the home being advertised for $20,000 per month by October 26, 2026."

On Nov. 6, the rental property was taken off the market.

The suit alleges that Compass and Bornstein, its listing agent for the second property, discriminated against Bakambu and Hueber by failing to consider or negotiate their offer because of familial status, and that this was in retaliation for Bakambu and Hueber raising fair-housing concerns regarding negotiations for the first property.

While this was going on, Bakambu's family was forced to remain in temporary housing at his own expense, according to the filing.

The filing reads: "Cédric and Anne allege that this sequence was not [an] ordinary rental negotiation. They were denied equal consideration because their household included five children, and Compass subjected them to further adverse treatment after they asserted their fair-housing rights.

"The consequences were concrete: lost housing opportunities, additional expenses, prolonged housing instability, disruption of efforts to arrange schooling and activities for their children, humiliation, and emotional distress."

stories.headline: From an ACL tear to a time trial PB: Koby LeCras on building resilience in his draft year
stories.summary: Rangey wing-forward Koby LeCras saw a breakout year derailed by a partially torn ACL, but six weeks back running was enough to deliver a personal-best 2km time. He talks to Jasper Chellappah about his recovery and future ahead of the 2026 AFL Draft.
stories.body:
Koby LeCras wasn't expected to test at the AFL Draft combine. He also wasn't expected to be named best afield amongst the premier prospects of the 2026 draft class, or make his senior WAFL debut in his dad's No. 20 for West Perth.

It was a blazing start to his season that put the nephew of former West Coast forward Mark firmly in first-round contention. From there it all unravelled.

LeCras suffered a partially torn ACL in that WAFL debut. Senior football, the national championships, and flag tilts were all wiped away. It was a cruel end to a year that promised so much.

But the teenager was desperate to get back for something on his calendar, and the final destination for all draft hopefuls is the combine.

Despite just six weeks of training post-injury, LeCras turned out for the 2km time trial. He ran a 6:23, good for a top-15 time and a personal best under heavy duress.

"Going into it I had 6:25 written on my hand, so I got away with a couple seconds," LeCras told ESPN.

"When I started running it was the goal to do the 2km and the 20m sprint at the combine. I knew what the plan was, where I was going to be and what I was going to do."

Worries had been lurking at the back of Lecras's mind. He avoided surgery on the partial tear but it was difficult for him to regain 100% confidence in his knee when he got back to running.

"You look at Gryan Miers, you can rush it back. Being your draft year and you've obviously got a lot more footy to play than just this year [West Perth] were pretty quick to shut that down, that I wasn't going to play again.

"I just wanted to get back as quick as I could, whether it was combine or day one of pre-season. They said 'Yeah you can do the combine and then definitely back for day one of pre-season'."

LeCras's injury was devastating timing given the showing he'd treated recruiters to the previous week. Off a wing, the 192cm utility was best afield for the AFL Academy - a representative side featuring the best of the draft class thrown together against VFL opposition.

LeCras kicked three goals from 19 disposals and nine marks, commanding the air and showing off that aerobic endurance in defence and attack.

It was a performance reminiscent of Ollie Dempsey's ability to capitalise on mismatches with his strong hands in marking contests and sniff out opportunities in dangerous areas.

LeCras was delivering on the next evolution of the winger in the AFL, but he was playing up the ground out of team need and still sees himself as a forward 50 threat.

"I think I'm a natural forward, but I'm open to playing anywhere, whether it's halfback, wing, hopefully inside one day maybe.

"I love watching specific players, I'm probably a bit of a nuff.

"I love watching Jeremy Cameron, I reckon he's a superstar. And then obviously Logan Morris as well, sort of that undersized key forward. I love what he does and how he finds ways to beat his defenders. He's a freak, he's next level."

Koby's uncle Mark LeCras is one of the more underrated small forwards to play in the modern era. The one club player booted 441 goals from 219 games, and was the oldest player in the Eagles's 2018 triumph before retiring.

Similarly to his uncle, Koby is adept at twisting onto his preferred left foot and finding the goals from uncanny positions. He possesses natural forward craft, from leading patterns at challenging size to match up on to a natural, repeatable set shot action and goal nous from tight angles.

While his dad Brent enjoyed his own 141-game WAFL career, Koby's uncle continues to be a wealth of information as he prepares to step up to the AFL level.

"He's been massive. In the pre-season I watched a lot of vision with him, little ways to improve my game," LeCras said.

"If I could be half the player he was, I'd be really happy with that."

Mark's best day came against Essendon in 2010 at Etihad Stadium, kicking 12 goals straight. He booted 46 goals from 15 games against the Bombers in his career.

"We always joke about that, if he played against Essendon every week he would've kicked a thousand. That's what he reckons!"

stories.headline: Wings' Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd talk relationship on pod
stories.summary: Azzi Fudd hosted Wings teammate Paige Bueckers on her podcast and the two discussed their relationship, Dallas' season and Fudd's recovery from knee surgery.
stories.body:
Dallas Wings teammates Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers, the past two WNBA No. 1 draft picks, spoke on Fudd's podcast Friday about a variety of topics, including a personal life update.

"We're not together anymore; it's been a while," Bueckers said on the "Fudd Around and Find Out" podcast. "[We] share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Bueckers and Fudd, who were teammates in college at UConn, said they felt the need to address their relationship status in part because of allegations it factored into the Wings picking Fudd at No. 1 in April. Fudd was chosen over TCU guard Olivia Miles, who went on to be the Rookie of the Year for the Minnesota Lynx. Spain's Awa Fam (Seattle Storm) was taken third, followed by teammates from the 2026 champion UCLA Bruins: Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics), Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) and Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo).

Fudd, Fam, Betts and Miles were all No. 1 at different points in ESPN's mock draft in the months before the April draft. Bueckers said her previous relationship with Fudd had no impact on Dallas' decision.

"We were not together before she got drafted," Bueckers said. "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points but was limited to just 30 games after an injury to her right knee led to season-ending arthroscopic surgery in August. She offered an update on her health.

"My offseason's been good," Fudd said. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy.

"I think there's a lot I can improve on. Especially the iso game; I feel like I'm not too comfortable with that yet. I know I'm capable of doing a little bit more. Watching someone like Paige who is able to create from anywhere ... that's great inspiration for me."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists, and was named to the All-WNBA second team as Dallas reached the playoffs as the No. 7 seed.

The Wings were eliminated in the first round by the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries. Bueckers said she learned a lot from her first playoff experience and complimented Golden State.

"The Valkyries' defense, I can't explain to you how tough they are," Bueckers said. "They swarm, they send bodies, they trap you, they blitz you, they're so connected. I'm glad I got to have that experience against them to open my eyes to what the playoffs are like -- the physicality, the pressure, the environment.

"And I'm proud of our season. I hated losing; I sat and was pissed about it for like a week. I reached out to [Sue Bird] about it, what was her first playoff experience like. I didn't play as well as I wanted to. But it was my first experience, going against a really good opponent, and I was learning and growing through it all."

Fudd and Bueckers also addressed the Wings' move to the 19,000-seat American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas next season after playing at UT Arlington's College Park Center, which seats over 7,000, since the franchise relocated to Texas in 2016.

"UTA was a vibe; we had a ball, we did our thing there," Bueckers said. "But definitely excited to move into Dallas. New times."

While the change in venue will lead to more eyes on Wings games, the two players said they're hoping for less scrutiny of any on-court behavior.

Both said fans shouldn't read into interactions the two have with each other or their teammates as anything other than normal team behavior. They also said they don't stand for "hate of any kind" or "tearing people down to lift us up."

"We've seen a lot of negativity," Bueckers said. "We've had stuff sent to us, stuff sent to our family, our friends. There's been some crazy things said about us. We still support each other, we're still going to be great friends, we're still going to be great teammates. All the negative things can be put aside, and you don't need to overanalyze everything."

Fudd added with a chuckle, "Also, we don't need messages [from fans] on what the other person's doing. We've addressed everything we need to, and the rest will stay with us."

stories.headline: Jillaroos make shock halves call for World Cup final
stories.summary: Brisbane's Jesse Southwell has replaced Jocelyn Kelleher in the Jillaroos side for the World Cup final as New Zealand make one key change to their men's team.
stories.body:
Australia have recalled Brisbane star Jesse Southwell at five-eighth and dropped Sydney Roosters premiership winner Jocelyn Kelleher for the Women's World Cup final.

It is a big call by Jillaroos coach Jess Skinner ahead of the showdown with the Kiwi Ferns on Sunday at Suncorp Stadium, after Kelleher played in three of the four matches won by Australia in the tournament.

Kelleher was also player of the match at No.6 in the 40-0 win over Samoa on Test debut in the opening round.

Southwell, who will partner Tarryn Aiken in the halves, did shine in the record-breaking 124-6 win over Wales where she had a personal haul of 44 points from a try and 20 goals from 21 attempts.

She was also a key in NSW's 3-0 series win over Queensland in this year's State of Origin series.

Kelleher also kicks goals and shared a strong bond with Roosters teammate and halfback Aiken during their NRLW title win, but has been named in the 21 jersey for the clash with New Zealand.

Try whiz Jaime Chapman has been picked on the wing, despite coming from the field early with a hamstring issue in the 30-14 win over Fiji in the semi-final.

The Ferns have retained the same 17 that defeated Samoa 32-0 in their semi.

New Zealand men's team, meantime, have recalled winger Ronaldo Mulitalo from suspension to the starting side for the final showdown with Australia on Sunday night.

Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad has made way after he scored a try in the 34-10 semi-final win over Tonga.

Mulitalo was sent off in the 72-0 win over Fiji for a shoulder charge and copped a one-match ban.

Australia have named the same 19 that beat Samoa 44-12 for the decider.

Centre Latrell Mitchell and half Sam Walker have been listed at No.18 and No.19 respectively with coach Kevin Walters settling on Bradman Best as his left centre and Tom Dearden at No.7, both of whom were outstanding against Samoa.

stories.headline: U.S. Supreme Court won't hear dispute over Clemente license plates in P.R.
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to take up a dispute between Roberto Clemente's sons vs. Puerto Rico over the use of the legend's image on license plates.
stories.body:
The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday declined to take up a dispute between Roberto Clemente's sons against Puerto Rico over the use of the baseball legend's image and name on commemorative license plates and registration tags released in 2022 and discontinued that same year.

The appeal was by Clemente's sons, Roberto Clemente Jr, Luis Roberto Clemente and Roberto Enrique Clemente, against the Puerto Rico government, claiming that the use of the Hall of Famer's unauthorized likeness, which generated $15 million for Puerto Rico, breached constitutional protections in the Fifth Amendment against a government taking of private property by seizing trademark rights.

The lawsuit, Clemente Properties v. Pierluisi-Urrutia, asked the courts to halt all future use of Clemente's image on plates and tags while seeking $45 million in damages alongside $3.15 million in compensation for trademark infringement.

"A Supreme Court decision in favor of the Clementes would have not only vindicated the rights of Roberto Clemente's family, but would have also strengthened constitutional protections for name, image, and likeness for athletes across the country," Wen Fa, an attorney for the sons, told ESPN in a statement. "Although we are disappointed by the Court's decision not to hear the important issues presented by our petition, we look forward to litigating the remaining claims in the trial court."

Born in Carolina, Puerto Rico, Roberto Clemente played 18 seasons in right field for the Pittsburgh Pirates, from 1955 to 1972.

He was a 15-time All-Star and two-time ​World Series champion. He died at age 38 in a 1972 airplane crash while delivering humanitarian aid to ​earthquake victims in Nicaragua. He was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1973.

The lawsuit was dismissed by San Juan U.S. District Judge Gina Méndez-Miró, and the Boston-based 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals partially upheld that decision, dismissing the argument that Puerto Rico's use of the trademarks amounted to an unconstitutional taking.

In a filing to the Supreme Court, lawyers for the ​sons said that the lower courts improperly concluded that the Fifth Amendment does ​not automatically apply ⁠to intangible property like trademarks.

"Left unanswered, the 1st Circuit's ruling would invite government to take trademarks on demand -- checked only by a multi-factor balancing test that allows government to destroy much in value and pay nothing in return," they ⁠wrote.
